# Set Similarity Metrics

Three ways to turn "how alike are these two sets?" into a number between 0 and 1. The optional task
of lab 3 in [[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] codes all three and applies them to a job
recommender, which is what makes the differences visible rather than academic.

| Metric | Formula | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Jaccard** | `\|A∩B\| / \|A∪B\|` | penalises every non-shared element; strict |
| **Sørensen–Dice** | `2\|A∩B\| / (\|A\|+\|B\|)` | double-weights the overlap; more forgiving of size mismatch |
| **Cosine** (on sets) | `\|A∩B\| / √(\|A\|·\|B\|)` | geometric mean in the denominator; between the other two |

Dice and Jaccard are monotone transforms of each other, so they rank pairs identically — they differ
only in the *magnitude* of the score, which matters as soon as a threshold is applied. Cosine can
reorder pairs when the two sets differ sharply in size, because a large set is penalised by `√` rather
than linearly.

## The application

A skill-set recommender: user skills as one set, job requirements as another.

- **Skill gap** = `requirements − skills`, a set difference read directly as "what to learn next".
- **Match category** = a banded label over the similarity score.
- **Composite score** = job match × mean similarity to similar users × count of similar users —
  a collaborative-filtering shape built from nothing but set operations.

That composite is the interesting part: three quantities multiplied with no weighting, so a single
zero factor annihilates the recommendation.

## A wrinkle worth recording

This optional task uses Python's **builtin** `set`, while `mandatory_tasks/core.py` in the same lab
implements `Set`, `MultiSet` and `EmptySet` from scratch over native lists (see
[[characteristic-functions]]). Whether the mandatory task forbade builtins or this is drift is not
recorded in the repo. **TODO:** unresolved; `confidence: low` on the reason.
